# GetGraphicsHDR <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [World](Blitz3D-World)

</div>


```blitzbasic
GetGraphicsHDR:Void Out mode:Int32=0, Out minimum:Float32=0, Out average:Float32=0, Out maximum:Float32=0
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | Out | Int32 | `0` | The mode. |
| `minimum` | Out | Float32 | `0` | The darkest value in nits. |
| `average` | Out | Float32 | `0` | The brightness of SDR white in nits. |
| `maximum` | Out | Float32 | `0` | The brightest value in nits. |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

A BlitzLLVM extension: gives back what [SetGraphicsHDR](SetGraphicsHDR) is set to. The brightness of SDR white and the peak are the ones in use, so they are the ones of the system when none was set. Arguments that are left out are not written.
